title: Testing a release boost in STXBP1 neurons

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding; its weakest link is the shared-pathway connection to aminopyridines combined with uncertainty about the direction of STXBP1 release defects.
Test whether 4-aminopyridine restores evoked neurotransmitter release in neurons with reduced release, without increasing spontaneous release or network hyperexcitability.
Prioritize Stxbp1+/- neurons using the listed haploinsufficient mouse models, then patient iPSC neurons.
Ask the lab to confirm access and measurement capabilities; if suitable patient iPSC neurons are unavailable, that model would need to be established before that arm begins.
Establish the baseline release defect, then compare evoked release, spontaneous release and network hyperexcitability with and without 4-aminopyridine.
Use untreated neurons from the same model as the primary comparison, and keep mouse-model and patient-neuron results separate.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Stop this approach if network hyperexcitability appears; do not advance a condition that increases spontaneous release.
A clean rescue would justify further variant-stratified cell experiments, not treatment in patients.
The graph contains no study testing this therapy class in STXBP1-related disorders, and pathway participation does not establish benefit.
Do not generalize any rescue to variants without a demonstrated reduction in release.
